name: libmicrohttpd
listed_description: Small library that makes it easy to run an HTTP server as part of another application.
reason: No numeric comparison against a named incumbent. Opened the unofficial GitHub mirror Karlson2k/libmicrohttpd (README: binary about 30-40k when size-optimised, no benchmark data). gnu.org and git.gnunet.org were blocked by egress policy. A WebSearch snippet of the manual says an epoll thread pool with 4 threads exceeded 45,000 connections per second on loopback with Apache Benchmark, but that compares MHD's own select against epoll, not another server. No shootout found that includes it (the C++ REST framework benchmark compares cpprestsdk, restbed, pistache and PHP only).

name: libnl
listed_description: Collection of libraries providing APIs to the Linux kernel netlink protocol interfaces.
reason: Netlink library, not an HTTP server; guessed category was wrong. github.com/thom311/libnl page (LGPL-2.1, 490 stars) and raw ChangeLog have no benchmark, speed or performance numbers. A search for libnl versus libmnl found only qualitative statements that libmnl is more minimal, no numbers.

name: libpcap
listed_description: API provides to various kernel packet capture mechanism. BSD-3-Clause.
reason: Packet capture library; it is the incumbent baseline that other capture frameworks compare against, not a challenger. Raw README.md, CHANGES and doc/README.linux contain no benchmark or speedup numbers (grep for faster, speed, perform, throughput, benchmark found only timestamp and link-speed hits).

name: libquic
listed_description: A QUIC protocol library extracted from Chromium's QUIC Implementation.
reason: github.com/devsisters/libquic (BSD-3-Clause, 1.8k stars) README has no benchmark numbers and no comparison with nghttp3 or any other QUIC stack; it only says QUIC is experimental and aims to reduce latency versus TCP. Any published QUIC-versus-TCP numbers belong to Google's Chromium QUIC, not this extraction.

name: libquickmail
listed_description: Library intended to give developers a way to send e-mail (with attachments) from C/C++ programs.
reason: Email-sending library (GPL-3.0, last release 0.1.30 on 2023-05-04). The SourceForge project page has no benchmark or comparison with libcurl SMTP or any other mail library.

name: librdkafka
listed_description: Apache Kafka client library for C and C++.
reason: Only claim is README text 'current figures exceed 1 million msgs/second for the producer and 3 million msgs/second for the consumer': absolute figures, no named baseline, no hardware, no flags. Raw README.md, INTRODUCTION.md, the wiki index and the Performance wiki page have no comparison against the Java client or any other client. The confluent-kafka-python README only says it significantly outperforms pure Python clients, with no numbers (the 5-10x figure seen via WebSearch comes from a content-farm snippet about the Python binding, not librdkafka itself). Third-party Go shootouts (franz-go claims) show librdkafka-based confluent-kafka-go slower, not faster.

name: libsagui
listed_description: Library for cross-platform HTTP servers. LGPL-3.0-or-later.
reason: github.com/risoflora/libsagui (94 stars) README only says it is 'so fast, compact and useful' because it builds on GNU libmicrohttpd; no benchmark, req/s figure or comparison with another server. Project site is on github.io, blocked by egress policy. Directional claim without numbers, not notable enough for a tier D record.
